findings.text: blocking: ruff format --check on the staged test file exits non-zero and would reformat the block added at :148-155, while the base revision's copy of the same file is already formatted, so the done_when's "Ruff check and ruff format --check add no findings on the staged paths" is unmet and no ruff log exists to have caught it.

non-blocking: the added assertions do not distinguish the index-free read from the indexed one -- :296 builds the ledger index from the just-promoted document with the default ledger.load and :298 then calls the guard, so restoring use_index=True at reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:3373 leaves every case passing; no fixture ever leaves a stale index for the guard to disagree with.

non-blocking: the "Fresh trees" paragraph reports 56 passed at the revision whose failure was reported as though that were the reproduction, but logs/repro-224-clean.log and logs/repro-224-hostile.log both record 56 passed EXIT=0 at 224dc0f7b3, so the reported release was never reproduced and the index explanation at :59 is an untested hypothesis rather than an observed cause.

non-blocking: the index-free read walks the aggregate and every per-run document on each pass instead of reusing the warm index, and the guard's promoted branch then repeats that same walk inside runs._unloaded_sections, so a section whose run was promoted pays two full ledger scans per pass per waiting request while the fragment's "Cost" paragraph at docs/evidence/fragments/a-queue-holds-the-whole-plan/a-section-wait-releases-when-its-upstream-lands-not-when-it.html:67 still describes the cached read.
